items.title: 68357_Jimmy Maxwell oral history interview
items.q: I took them home to my house and my mother gave them all dinner... Buck and Jonah were sitting down in my studio one day and we were talking about playing trumpet.

ctx.x: Sure did. That road traveling was kind of rough. You know, I remember Cab Calloway's band, years later when things got to be good, he'd still organize little basketball teams, you know. Or football or baseball teams. And I guess this was an outgrowth of those times when a band hit town and there was no gig. You just organized as a baseball team and play the local guys.

Well, that's the way it worked with those bands. I remember, you know, bands being down on their luck. This was after I'd gone down to Los Angeles about 1936 or '37. I saw four or five familiar faces standing around the street in Tracy one day and one of them said, aren't you Buck Clayton? And he said, yeah. He said, what are you doing here? He said, I'm here with my band and the promoters run out. No money and everything so they had Buck Clayton, Lee Young and about six of the others. They said they hadn't eaten…
The bands would travel. They'd just go up the coast and come down and say, look, you know, you've got a hall. We'll put on a dance for a certain percentage.
